_meta.note: Candidate diplomacy rules for the AUCA and PROD game actors, disaggregated into six real governments. Companion to resources.md. Proposed game mechanics, NOT measured acceptance probabilities and NOT evidence of any government's consent.
_meta.owner: research area 4 (Australia, Canada and producer states, disaggregated)
design_rules: No rule grants automatic approval; every rule yields an explicit state with reasons.
No invented acceptance odds; responses are deterministic preconditions the player can inspect.
food/medicine tokens never flip a mineral or hosting decision (see resources.md section 3).
A government letter binds its own instruments (licences, funding stages, JV terms), not foreign-owned plants or refiners.

rules.actor: Australian Government (PM&C Office of AI; Parliament for the bill)
rules.objective: Host accord compute/conditions and license mineral inputs on Australia's terms
rules.authority_instrument: Planned AI Standards legislation (not yet law); national Expectations of data centres and AI infrastructure developers (Mar 2026); FIRB/FATA screening; SOCI Act
rules.trigger: Player tables an accord condition needing Australian hosting or Australian mineral inputs
rules.conditions: Offer must include an energy package (new firmed generation + full connection costs, mirroring the standards' own requirement) plus value-capture commitments (skills/research/processing)
rules.time_cost: Any yes before the bill passes is a commitment to legislate; window 'early 2027'; letter carries 'subject to Parliament passing the AI Standards bill'
rules.substitute: Route through government procurement or a facility the operator voluntarily builds (CPTPP Art. 14.13 constrains local-compute mandates)
rules.evidence_limit: Bill text does not exist yet; thresholds and duties still under consultation as of Oct 2026

rules.objective: Value capture on minerals and frontier-training deals
rules.authority_instrument: AI-training conditions track in the planned standards; Future Made in Australia industrial-strategy framing
rules.conditions: Local processing / skills / research rider attached to the deal
rules.time_cost: rider negotiation adds at least one month
rules.substitute: None: rider is the stated price of 'AI investments on Australia's terms'
rules.evidence_limit: Rider is a design proposal grounded in retrieved policy direction, not a quoted statutory clause; specific minerals-processing incentives (e.g. CMPTI) were not retrievable this pass (industry.gov.au/ato.gov.au blocked)

rules.objective: Join an accord and open Canadian compute to its conditions
rules.authority_instrument: Sovereign AI Compute Strategy programs (SCIP open; AI Compute Challenge; Access Fund) and staged public investment agreements (announced Cohere equity, vehicle unknown)
rules.trigger: Player offers capital + market, or an anchor compute-purchase commitment
rules.conditions: Offer structured in stages with public progress reporting (jobs/compute), mirroring the real staged announcement; first tranche only on signature
rules.time_cost: at least one month between offer and signed agreement
rules.substitute: Buy Canadian compute commercially and attach conditions contractually
rules.evidence_limit: Cohere investing vehicle, signatory and draw conditions unknown at cutoff; no rule may assume Canada controls Cohere; AIDA's fate unverified (Canada must not be shown with an AI act)

rules.authority_instrument: AI Safety Institute of Canada (Budget 2024: $50M over five years); institute cooperation
rules.trigger: Accord goal is testing or incident definition/sharing
rules.conditions: Implementation routed through CAISI + AI-institute cooperation; no unilateral national veto over a developer
rules.time_cost: institute protocols take months; no instant reciprocity
rules.substitute: Bilateral evaluation-recognition agreement instead of coalition-wide accession
rules.evidence_limit: CAISI launch date and leadership not verified this pass; Budget 2024 only proposed the institute

rules.actor: DRC Government (Presidency; Ministry of Mines; ARECOMS)
rules.objective: Join a minerals-linked accord at its stated price
rules.authority_instrument: ARECOMS export licences/quotas (cobalt ban decree of 22 Feb 2025; quotas reported Sep 2025); 2018 mining-code strategic-substance regime
rules.trigger: Player asks DRC to attach conditions to cobalt/copper flows
rules.conditions: Offer must contain a security component or corridor/energy-infrastructure finance (the DRC's publicly stated price in US negotiations; the game has no security token, so DRC answers 'not now' to food/medicine/capital alone and says what it wants)
rules.time_cost: months (its own controls took a full ministerial decree cycle)
rules.plausible_response: not_now_with_stated_price | yes_with_quota_terms if the offer matches
rules.substitute: none within the current token set; the gap is itself the finding
rules.evidence_limit: Whether a US-DRC minerals-for-security agreement was ever signed by cutoff was NOT established by retrieval; current quota terms unverified (Le Monde paywalled); ARECOMS founding date disputed between sources

rules.objective: Scope any accord commitment honestly to licences
rules.authority_instrument: Export licences and quota terms; artisanal/industrial separation decree shows licence-level micro-regulation style
rules.trigger: Accord asks for supply-chain guarantees beyond DRC borders
rules.conditions: DRC promises licence-level conditions only (reporting, traceability, destination disclosure)
rules.time_cost: licence amendments per cycle, not instant
rules.plausible_response: accepts_licence_terms | cannot_promise_refined_supply (refining sits elsewhere in the chain)
rules.evidence_limit: Production is largely foreign-owned (CMOC, Glencore); team's layers.json shares mark refining concentration outside DRC

rules.actor: Indonesian Government (ESDM; mining-law framework; Mind ID)
rules.objective: Mineral cooperation only via onshore processing
rules.authority_instrument: Export ban + domestic processing requirement (in force ~7-9 years at the 2022 WTO panel; appeal into the void since 8 Dec 2022)
rules.trigger: Any accord clause treating Indonesian output as a raw-material lever
rules.conditions: Player must offer onshore-processing investment (capital + technology/local-value commitment) so the clause supports the DPR rather than bypassing it
rules.time_cost: immediate no on raw-ore asks; months of licence/contract work otherwise
rules.substitute: Deal structured on processed products (battery-supply-chain ambition is the stated end goal)
rules.evidence_limit: Reported 2025 refined-nickel export-duty plan not verified this pass; data-centre/AI posture not retrieved (Microsoft Apr 2024 commitment known by name only)

rules.objective: Environmental and social sustainability of any cooperation
rules.authority_instrument: Deal-level obligations co-funded by the player (design proposal)
rules.conditions: Environmental/social obligations (deforestation, smelter-community impacts) co-funded as part of the package
rules.time_cost: adds review time to any yes
rules.evidence_limit: Documented friction is real (2024 deforestation reporting), but no retrieved Indonesian instrument enforces deal-level obligations; this is a design proposal

rules.actor: Chilean Government (CORFO; Codelco; ENAMI; Contraloria approves contracts)
rules.objective: Lithium-linked accord participation through state-controlled vehicles
rules.authority_instrument: National Lithium Strategy (2023, in force): no ordinary concession; state controlling interest in new strategic projects; partners cede share and pay royalties; JV contracts (Nova Andino Litio created 30 Dec 2025; Contraloria approval reported 6 Feb 2026)
rules.conditions: Player accepts a state-controlled JV with royalties; private direct offers are redirected, not refused
rules.time_cost: months (real JV path: agreement to company creation to comptroller approval)
rules.plausible_response: join_us_in_the_vehicle | not_now if player insists on private terms
rules.substitute: Cooperation on copper or hosting does not require the JV path
rules.evidence_limit: gob.cl blocked for this client; JV dates verified via tertiary read citing the primary announcement; internal JV economics not public here

rules.objective: Water and community protection as deal gates
rules.authority_instrument: Strategy pillars: Protected Salt Flats Network (>=30% of these ecosystems by 2030); Public Technology and Research Institute; stakeholder engagement process
rules.conditions: Water monitoring and protected-area terms included; Atacama water science shown as contested, not settled
rules.time_cost: community/engagement process runs months to years
rules.plausible_response: accepts_with_water_terms | stalls in review without them
rules.evidence_limit: Protected Salt Flats Network is strategy-track policy; no retrieved enforcement instrument; the SQM freshwater-inflow dispute is documented as unresolved

rules.actor: Peruvian Government (new Fujimori administration; Ministry of Energy and Mines; Congress)
rules.objective: Mining-linked accord participation under stability terms
rules.authority_instrument: Legal-stability contract regime and fiscal regime (structural, survives governments); Congress ratification (no party holds majorities: Senate 22/60, Chamber 41/130)
rules.conditions: Player guarantees stability-style terms (no surprise fiscal changes for the deal's life) plus infrastructure/capital investment
rules.time_cost: long; letter carries 'Congress has not ratified' state
rules.substitute: Cooperation through existing operator contracts rather than new state deals
rules.evidence_limit: Election result is certified fact (Fujimori 50.13%, certified 29 Jun 2026) but the new government's mineral/AI positions are NOT established by retrieval; treat any specific stance as fictional and marked; inauguration date unverified

rules.objective: Community consent as a gate on mineral cooperation
rules.authority_instrument: Canon minero redistribution (50% of mining income tax to producing regions); consultation/community processes; documented corporate-community conflict pattern
rules.conditions: Community/prior-consultation guarantees included; projects stall where communities resist, regardless of capital
rules.time_cost: conflict lines can stall projects indefinitely
rules.evidence_limit: Underlying read is explicitly outdated (needs-update banner; 2006-era structural data); current conflict lines not retrieved

cross_cutting_findings.medicine_food_finding: No retrieved source ties any of the six governments' AI-supply-chain bargaining to food or medicine offers. DRC is the sharpest case: US assistance exceeds $1bn/year and the DRC still restricted cobalt exports. Recommended game behaviour: food/medicine offers change tone, never answers.
cross_cutting_findings.prior_help_finding: Prior help works as a precondition that opens a specific door (energy co-funding for Australia; staged anchor investment for Canada; security/corridors for DRC; processing investment for Indonesia; JV acceptance for Chile; stability+community for Peru), never as a general bonus or odds boost.
cross_cutting_findings.public_private_finding: Government letters bind licences, funding stages and JV terms; physical capacity is often foreign/private (CMOC/Glencore in DRC; Chinese-owned smelters in Indonesia; SQM/Tianqi in Chile; Cohere in Canada; FIRB-screened operators in Australia). Scope letters to the actual instrument.

window_corrections.AUCA_window_is_australia_only: The 'AI Standards legislation planned for early 2027' window matches Australia; Canada's clocks are program-based (SCIP applications open now; staged Cohere payments with unknown draw dates).
window_corrections.prod_needs_medicine_first: game.js needs() makes the game offer medicine to PROD first; no retrieved evidence supports medicine as a decisive lever for any producer government.
